task: Who is the parent company of Rivian?

merged.claim: Rivian Automotive, Inc. has no parent company; it is an independent, publicly traded company, not a subsidiary.

variants.F: Rivian Automotive, Inc. has no parent company; it is an independent, publicly traded American automaker rather than a subsidiary.
variants.D: Rivian Automotive, Inc. is an independent, publicly traded company and not a subsidiary; it has no parent company.
variants.E: Rivian does not have a parent company; Rivian Automotive, Inc. is an independent publicly traded company.

merged.claim: Rivian's parent company is Rivian Automotive, Inc.

variants.A: Rivian's parent company is Rivian Automotive, Inc.

merged.claim: Rivian Automotive, Inc. is the parent of Rivian, LLC, a Delaware LLC described in the SEC filing (dated 2026-03-19) as its wholly-owned subsidiary.

variants.A: Rivian Automotive, Inc. is the parent company of Rivian, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company that the SEC filing describes as a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company (filing dated 2026-03-19).

merged.claim: The SEC filing dated 2026-03-19 names the registrant as Rivian Automotive, Inc.

variants.A: The SEC filing dated 2026-03-19 names the registrant as Rivian Automotive, Inc.

merged.claim: The filing uses "Rivian" as shorthand for the company and its consolidated subsidiaries, with Rivian Automotive, Inc. as the legal parent in the hierarchy.

variants.A: The filing uses "Rivian" as shorthand for the company and its consolidated subsidiaries, while the legal parent identified in the hierarchy is Rivian Automotive, Inc.

merged.claim: Rivian Automotive, Inc. was incorporated as a Delaware corporation on March 26, 2015.

variants.F: Rivian Automotive, Inc. was incorporated as a Delaware corporation on March 26, 2015.
variants.B: Rivian Automotive, Inc. (together with its consolidated subsidiaries) was incorporated as a Delaware corporation on March 26, 2015.

merged.claim: Rivian's common stock trades on Nasdaq under the ticker RIVN.

variants.F: Rivian's Class A common stock ($0.001 par value) trades on The Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker RIVN.
variants.E: Rivian Automotive, Inc. common stock trades on Nasdaq under the ticker RIVN.

merged.claim: Rivian files its own financial statements with the SEC, most recently its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.

variants.F: Rivian files its own financial statements with the SEC, most recently its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.

merged.claim: The no-parent conclusion reflects the corporate structure disclosed in Rivian's quarterly filing for the period ended September 30, 2026.

variants.E: The no-parent conclusion reflects the corporate structure disclosed in Rivian's quarterly filing for the period ended September 30, 2026.

merged.claim: Amazon (via Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC and Logistics) beneficially owns Rivian stock, including a warrant for 3,723,050 Class A shares, representing 10.9% of voting power as of July 10, 2026; a major shareholder, not a parent.

variants.F: Amazon (via Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC and Logistics) beneficially owns Rivian capital stock, including shares issuable on exercise of a warrant for 3,723,050 Class A shares, representing 10.9% of Rivian's voting power as of July 10, 2026; it is a major shareholder, not a parent.

merged.claim: Amazon is the parent of Logistics and Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC, which beneficially owns Rivian stock representing 10.8% of voting power as of September 30, 2026.

variants.B: Amazon is the parent company of Logistics and Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC, which beneficially owns Rivian capital stock representing 10.8% of Rivian's voting power as of September 30, 2026.

merged.claim: Amazon, the top Rivian holder since the 2021 IPO, is now the second-largest shareholder at about 12.28%.

variants.C: Amazon, the top Rivian holder since the 2021 IPO, is now the second-largest shareholder at about 12.28%.

merged.claim: Volkswagen and Amazon are significant shareholders in Rivian, not its parent companies.

variants.D: Volkswagen and Amazon are major shareholders in Rivian, not parent companies.
variants.B: Volkswagen AG and Amazon are significant shareholders of Rivian, not its parent.

merged.claim: Volkswagen is Rivian's largest shareholder at roughly 15.9% as of May 2026 (secondary-source estimate), but Rivian remains independently run with its own board and CEO.

variants.F: Volkswagen is Rivian's largest shareholder at roughly 15.9% as of May 2026 (secondary-source estimate), but Rivian remains independently run with its own board and CEO.

merged.claim: Volkswagen-US Holding, Inc. (formerly Volkswagen International America, Inc.), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Volkswagen AG, beneficially owns Rivian shares representing 14.1% of voting power as of July 10, 2026, a large minority stake rather than control.

variants.F: Volkswagen-US Holding, Inc. (formerly Volkswagen International America, Inc.), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Volkswagen AG, beneficially owns Rivian shares representing 14.1% of voting power as of July 10, 2026, a large minority stake rather than a controlling interest.

variants.B: Volkswagen-US Holding, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Volkswagen AG, beneficially owned shares of Rivian capital stock representing 14.0% of Rivian's voting power as of September 30, 2026.

variants.C: One forum-posted table lists Volkswagen's Rivian stake at 16.64%, differing slightly from the 15.9% figure.

c1.note: Rivian is independent and publicly traded, with no parent. VW (15.9%) and Amazon (about 12%) are shareholders only.

c5.note: Rivian Automotive, Inc. is the company itself, not its own parent. The question's answer is that no parent exists.

c6.note: The 8-K names Rivian, LLC as a party. The wholly-owned subsidiary status is not in the excerpt but matches known structure.

c7.note: The 8-K names Rivian Automotive, Inc. as the registrant. The event date is March 18, with a press release on March 19.

c8.note: The 10-Q uses 'Rivian' as shorthand for Rivian Automotive, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries.

c9.note: The 10-Q states incorporation as a Delaware corporation on March 26, 2015.

c10.note: The 10-Q cover page lists Class A common stock under RIVN on Nasdaq.

c11.note: Rivian does file its own statements, but the most recent 10-Q covers the quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (signed Oct 29, 2026), not June 30.

c12.note: The Q3 10-Q shows Rivian as the top registrant with consolidated subsidiaries and no parent.

c15.note: A Schedule 13G/A shows VW at 15.9% and Amazon second at 12.28%. Amazon was the earliest major backer.

c16.note: Rivian is independent and publicly traded; VW and Amazon are shareholders, not parents.

c17.note: VW at about 15.9% and largest shareholder, corroborated by the Schedule 13G/A report; Rivian stays independently run.

c19.note: The 10-Q confirms the Volkswagen-US Holding name change; the 14.1% voting figure is not in the passages but is plausible given dilution from the July offering, and the minority stake conclusion holds.

c20.note: The Q3 10-Q covers the VW-US Holding relationship; 14.0% as of Sept 30 is consistent with the 14.1% in July and subsequent dilution, though the exact figure is not in the passages.

c21.note: 10-Q states the JV was established in November 2024 with a focus on software, ECUs and network architecture.

c23.note: Rivian's 10-Q dated Oct 29, 2026 describes the JV and VW's committed equity investments subject to milestones.

c24.note: Filings show VW as an equity investor and JV partner with a minority stake, not a parent.

c26.note: The 10-Q reports regulatory credit and software revenues from VW Group; a significant share is consistent with Rivian's filings, though the passages don't state the share.

c27.note: The 10-Q refers to Robert J. Scaringe as Founder and CEO.

c28.note: The wording is garbled, but EVwire says the stake rose to 15.9% from 8.6% less than two years earlier.

c29.note: The EVwire article is dated Jul 6, 2026.

c30.note: EVwire states a $5.8B total commitment in milestone-based tranches, with the stake contractually set to rise.

c32.note: The rest is held across public float and institutions, none above 5% disclosed; the largest holders (VW 15.9%, Amazon 12.28%) are well below majority.

c34.note: Source names Oryx Global as the vehicle of Abdul Latif Jameel, so the naming difference is real but trivial; the caveat is reasonable.

c35.note: Schedule 13G is the short-form filing for passive holders under SEC rules, consistent with a minority non-controlling stake.

c13.note: The 2026 proxy confirms Amazon, via NV Holdings, holds 3,723,050 warrant shares and is a shareholder, not a parent. I could not find the 10.9% voting-power figure or the July 10 date in the saved pages.

c14.note: NV Holdings is a wholly-owned Amazon subsidiary that holds Rivian stock. I could not confirm the 10.8% figure or the Logistics entity in the saved 10-Q.

c25.note: The Q3 2026 10-Q says the equally owned joint venture is a separate legal entity with its own management and board of directors.

c33.note: A forum-posted table (Rivian Forums, May 2026) lists VW at 16.64% and Amazon at 12.56%. The SEC Schedule 13G/A figure is 15.9% (209,769,645 Class A shares), per the evwire page, which does not mention 16.64%. The claim that a forum table differs slightly is accurate.
